outcome: An enchantment card can be cast from hand only in a main phase of its controller's turn with an empty stack.
A resolving enchantment spell moves to the battlefield under its controller's control.
An Aura enters the battlefield attached to an object or player allowed by its enchant ability.
An Aura spell needs a legal target defined by its enchant ability to be cast.
An Aura enchanting an illegal or missing object or player is put into its owner's graveyard in the state-based check.
An Aura enchanting itself, or an Aura creature, is put into its owner's graveyard in the state-based check.
Changing control of an Aura or its enchanted object does not change the other's controller, and only the Aura's controller can activate its abilities.
An Aura entering with no legal object or player to enchant stays in its zone, or goes to the graveyard from the stack, or is not created as a token.
A permanent that is not an Aura, Equipment or Fortification put onto the battlefield attached to something enters unattached.
An Aura put onto the battlefield attached to an illegal or undefined object stays in its zone, or goes to the graveyard from the stack, or is not created as a token.
An effect attaching an Aura on the battlefield to an object it cannot legally enchant leaves the Aura where it is.
When a permanent has several Roles controlled by one player, all but the most recent are put into their owners' graveyards in the state-based check.
